# Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
```

# Data

```{r}
#| label: load-data
hfc_tib <- read_rds(str_c(
  "https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/kospnc09qscm43inp0jgk/",
  "hfc.rds?rlkey=a14kkpiha47hhjuyvn4ffswnj&dl=1"))
```

```{r}
#| label: clean-data
hfc_tib <- hfc_tib %>%
  arrange(store, product, date) %>%
  mutate(gross_profit = (price_retail - price_wholesale) * sales,
         price_id = consecutive_id(price_retail), .by = c(store, product)) %>%
  mutate(days_since_price_change = row_number(date) - 1,
         days_until_price_change = row_number(-as.integer(date)),
         .by = c(store, product, price_id)) %>%
  filter(price_id > 1)

horizon_length <- 90
post_change_mean_profit <- hfc_tib %>%
  filter(days_since_price_change <= horizon_length,
         n() >= horizon_length, .by = c(store, product, price_id)) %>%
  summarise(mean_profit = mean(gross_profit), .by = days_since_price_change)
```

# Period 1: Baseline (Current System)

*Menu cost = $0.40. What is HFC's optimal price duration and profit-per-day today?*

```{r}
#| label: period-1
menu_cost <- 0.40
net_ppd <- numeric(90)

for (d in 1:90) {
  profit_sum <- post_change_mean_profit %>%
    filter(days_since_price_change < d) %>%
    pull(mean_profit) %>%
    sum()

  net_ppd[d] <- (profit_sum - menu_cost) / d
}

optimal_d <- which.max(net_ppd)
cat("Optimal duration:", optimal_d, "days\n")
cat("Net profit per day:", round(net_ppd[optimal_d], 4), "\n")
```

# Period 2: ESL World

*Menu cost = $0.05. How does the optimal price duration and profit-per-day change?*

```{r}
#| label: period-2
menu_cost_esl <- 0.05
net_ppd_esl <- numeric(90)

for (d in 1:90) {
  profit_sum <- post_change_mean_profit %>%
    filter(days_since_price_change < d) %>%
    pull(mean_profit) %>%
    sum()

  net_ppd_esl[d] <- (profit_sum - menu_cost_esl) / d
}

optimal_d_esl <- which.max(net_ppd_esl)
cat("ESL optimal duration:", optimal_d_esl, "days\n")
cat("ESL net profit per day:", round(net_ppd_esl[optimal_d_esl], 4), "\n")
cat("Duration change:", optimal_d_esl - optimal_d, "days\n")
cat("Profit-per-day change:", round(net_ppd_esl[optimal_d_esl] - net_ppd[optimal_d], 4), "\n")
```

# Period 3: NPV and Recommendation

*Is the switch to ESLs worth it? Compute the NPV per product and stress-test the result.*

```{r}
#| label: period-3-npv
r <- 0.12
skus_per_store <- 50000

# Daily profit-per-day gain from switching to ESL
daily_gain_per_sku <- net_ppd_esl[optimal_d_esl] - net_ppd[optimal_d]

# Annualize, then take perpetuity value
annual_gain_per_sku <- daily_gain_per_sku * 365
pv_per_sku <- annual_gain_per_sku / r
pv_per_store <- pv_per_sku * skus_per_store

cat("Daily profit gain per SKU:  $", round(daily_gain_per_sku, 4), "\n")
cat("Annual profit gain per SKU: $", round(annual_gain_per_sku, 2), "\n")
cat("PV per SKU (break-even install cost): $", round(pv_per_sku, 2), "\n")
cat("PV per store:                         $", format(round(pv_per_store, 0), big.mark = ","), "\n")

# Stress test: vary discount rate from 8% to 16%
stress <- tibble(
  rate = seq(0.08, 0.16, by = 0.01),
  pv_per_sku = (annual_gain_per_sku) / rate,
  pv_per_store = pv_per_sku * skus_per_store
)
print(stress)

# Conservative stress test: profit gain overstated by 5x
install_cost_per_sku <- 12.00
conservative_annual_gain <- annual_gain_per_sku / 5
conservative_pv_per_sku <- conservative_annual_gain / r
conservative_npv_per_sku <- conservative_pv_per_sku - install_cost_per_sku

cat("\n--- Conservative Case (gain / 5, install = $12/SKU) ---\n")
cat("Annual gain per SKU (conservative): $", round(conservative_annual_gain, 2), "\n")
cat("PV per SKU:                         $", round(conservative_pv_per_sku, 2), "\n")
cat("NPV per SKU after $12 install:      $", round(conservative_npv_per_sku, 2), "\n")
cat("NPV per store:", format(round(conservative_npv_per_sku * skus_per_store, 0), big.mark = ","), "\n")
```

# Recommendation

HFC should install electronic shelf labels. The case for doing so does not rest primarily on labor savings — it rests on the value of repricing more frequently.

Under the current system, a \$0.40 menu cost pushes HFC toward longer pricing cycles. Every extra day a stale price rides, gross profit decays. ESLs drop that cost to \$0.05, shifting the optimal cycle shorter and keeping prices closer to where they should be. That repricing benefit — measured directly from HFC's own profit decay curve — is worth approximately \$59.80 per SKU at a 12% discount rate, or roughly \$3.0 million per store.

The stress test confirms the base case is compelling. At one-fifth the estimated demand lift and a \$12 per label install cost, the project is essentially breakeven — the downside scenario is not losing money, it is not gaining it. The math does not produce a meaningful loss until the benefit estimate is wrong by roughly 5x. That is not a realistic downside case; it is the boundary condition of the model.

The error in a purely cost-focused analysis is measuring only what ESLs save on labor. The larger value is what they recover in margin. Ignacio should authorize the install.
